This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Smt. Indramma W/o. Jagadeesh caused in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 20.05.2024 at about 6.45 a.m.
Mahadeva S/o. Raju was riding bike bearing Reg.No.KA-10-U-4709 along with deceased and deceased son to the hospital from Halguru to Golahalli Village on NH-209 bypass (Muthathi Road),
at that time on Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg. KA-04-AC-0348 goods vehicle driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner hit to back of the bike, due to impact, deceased Indramma fell down on the road and sustained severe injuries and Rohit Gowda also sustained injuries.
Immediately they were shifted to Govt. Hospital, Halaguru and then shifted to Mandya District Hospital for higher treatment and Indramma did not responded to the treatment and died on 20.05.2024.
Thereafter the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and conducted funeral and obsequies for which petitioners spent Rs.1,50,000/-.
Due to death of Indramma, petitioners lost the love and affection and also earning member of the family.
Hence pays to award compensation of Rs.40 lakhs from the respondents.
3. After service of notice to respondents, the respondents have appeared through their respective counsels and filed written statements.

4. The learned counsel for respondent No.1 has filed the objection statement wherein contended that this respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle and it was not driven by him on the date of accident.

Further the vehicle in which Indiramma was travelling was not driving by Mahadeva but by the minor son of the Indiramma that too no one was wearing the helmet while traveling and more than two persons are not allowed to be travelled in the two wheeler as stipulated by law and

Further there is no document has been produced to show that minor Rohit Gowda was suffering from fever and was taken to hospital and infact the two wheeler driven by the minor has entered the main road Jagadish vs Govindaraju on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77811601/
2 without observing the rules and was driven rashly and negligently as such the accident has occurred.

Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
5.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has filed the objection statement wherein contended that there is a violation of Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

This respondent has not issued a policy of insurance in favor of first respondent in respect of Bolero Pick up No.KA-04-AC- 0348 and the liability of this respondent company if any is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy and subject to valid and effective driving license of the driver and permit for the goods vehicle in question if the petitioner proves and furnishes the original policy of insurance covering the date of accident.

Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself who was riding the TP two wheeler without having proper look out of vehicular movements of the road and carelessly and due to his own negligence itself the accident occurred and not due to the negligence on the part of the driver of Bolero Pick Up.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings this tribunal has framed the following issues :

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased Indramma W/o. Jagadish died due to the grievous injury sustained by him in an accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Mahindra Bulero bearing No.KA-04-AC-0348 on 20.05.2024 at about 6.45 a.m. near Gollarahalli Road, Halaguru Bypass Road,
NH-209, Malavalli- Kanakapura Road, Mandya District and she succumbed to the said injuries?
2.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal representative of the deceased ?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award ?
7. The Petitioner No.1 got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Ex-P1 to 16 documents on behalf of the petitioners.
The respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
8. Arguments were addressed on both side.
9. Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS Jagadish vs Govindaraju on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77811601/
3 10
. ISSUE NO.1:

In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Ex-P1 to Ex-P16 i.e., FIR,
complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch, seizure mahazar, Inquest report, IMV report, PM report,
Charge sheet, Aadhar cards and PAN cards.
11.

On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.1 and 2 have filed the objections and respondent No.1 denied the entire petition taking contention that the accident has been taken place due to sole rash and negligent of the rider of the motorcycle as the rider of the motorcycle was proceeding in the motor cycle without wearing helmet and carrying more than 2 persons.

12. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 contended that the driver of the Bolero Pick up was not holding valid and effective DL at the time of accident and accident has been taken place due to sole rash and negligent on the part of the rider of the Two wheeler and was riding the motorcycle without having proper look out of vehicular movements of the road and carelessly and due to his own negligence itself the accident has been taken place and the rider of the motorcycle was riding the vehicle along with two pillion rider and due to his negligence lost control over the vehicle and caused the accident and the offending vehicle has not been involved in the accident and has been falsely implicated and prays to reject the petition.
13.

On perusal of evidence and materials on record, the accident has been taken place on 20.05.2024 at about 6.45 a.m. and thereafter on the same day one Sathish S/o. Puttaswamy Gowda father of petitioner lodged the complaint against the driver of the Mahindra Bolero Pick up as per Ex.P2.
Based on the said complaint, the jurisdictional Halagur Police registered the FIR as per Ex.P1.

Thereafter, the jurisdictional police have conducted thorough and detailed investigation and submitted charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle Bolero Pick up for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.187 of IMV Act and also filed charge sheet against the accused No.2 rider of the motorcycle for the offences punishable under Sec.128(1),
177, 146 R/W 196 of IMV Ac, by holding that on 20.05.2024 at about 6.45 a.m. when Mahadevu was proceeding in motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 10-U-4709 along with two pillion rider from Kanakapura towards Malavalli by passing over NH-209 HW on Halaguru Bypass road

, at that time,
the driver of Mahindra Goods vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the motorcycle while driver of the motorcycle crossing the Halaguru bypass road and thereby caused the accident.
Due to the accident, Indramma sustained grievous injuries and she was admitted to the Mandya District Hospital where the doctor declared her to be dead on the way.
Further Rohith Gowda petitioner No.3 who was also traveling as pillion rider in the motorcycle sustained grievous injuries and accordingly the investigating officer has filed the charge sheet.

14. On perusal of crime detailed form and Ex.P4 sketch it appears that the width of the road is 30 feet and the accident spot is a Junction where two interior road adjoin the main bypass road and accident has been taken place in the middle of the road when rider of the motorcycle Mahadevu was crossing the bypass road, at that time, the Bolero Pick up vehicle has hit to the motor cycle.
Ex. P3
and 4 clearly demonstrate that the accident has been taken place due to rash and negligence driving fo the driver of Bolero Pick up vehicle.

Though respondent contended that the accident has been taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle as the rider of motorcycle Jagadish vs Govindaraju on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77811601/
4 was running the motorcycle by carrying two pillion rider, but, no evidence and material brought on record by the respondent to show that the rider of the motorcycle was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner, unless any evidence is brought on record to prove the rash and negligence of the riding of the motorcycle by its rider.

Mere riding of the motorcycle along with two pillion rider does not itself amounts to rash and negligent driving, and it cannot be consider that deceased was riding motorcycle in rash and negligent manner.

Unless some evidence of rash and negligent is brought on record by respondent, it cannot be held that rider of motor cycle was riding motorcycle in rash and negligent manner, merely for reason he was riding bike with pillion rider.
15. Apart from this, respondents have not examined the driver of the Bolero Pick up vehicle who is material eye witness to disprove the evidence of the PW.1 and prove their contention.

Even the respondents have not examined Investigating officer to prove that the accident has not been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the Bolero Pick up vehicle and the charge sheet filed by the Investigating officer is collusive and defective.
Absolutely no evidence and materials brought on record by the respondents to prove that the charge sheet filed by the investigating officer is collusive and defective.

The very manner of the accident, coupled with the police documents clearly established that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

16. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
17. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
18. Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.

19. In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

sentences.text:
With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
20. ISSUES NO.2 : The petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed that he is the husband, petitioners No.2 and 3 are her children, petitioner No.4 is the mother of the Jagadish vs Govindaraju on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77811601/
5 deceased Indramma.

The documents which are exhibited at Ex's.P10 and 11, Ex.P13 to Ex.P15 -Adhaar cards reveals that the petitioner No.1 is the husband, petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children, petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased Indramma.
Hence issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative.
21. ISSUES NO.3:

From Ex-P10-Copy of adhaar card of Indramma, it reveals that date of birth of Indramma is 02.05.1988 and the accident has been taken place on 20.05.2024 and as on the date of accident, Indramma was aged 36 years.

Admittedly the deceased was married and the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group of 36 to 40 is '15'.
22.
The petitioners have stated that deceased Indramma was doing Hynugarike (dairy) and earning Rs.25,000/-p.m.
In support of their contentions, the petitioners have not produced any documents regarding the avocation and income of the deceased.
Therefore, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.

In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the deceased at the time of accident and nature of her work, if her income is assessed at Rs.16,500/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.

Hence, the annual income of the deceased will be considered as Rs.16,500/-.
23.

In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others),
the Hon'ble Apex Court held that addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in the absence of proof of income.

entities.text: 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand the deceased was aged 36 years.
24. As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SCC 5157, 40% of income is to be added towards future prospects in case of self employed.
40% of Rs.16,500/- works out to Rs.6,600/-.
Therefore the total income comes to Rs.23,100/- (16,500+6,600).
The deceased was married and having four dependents.
Hence 1/4 of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.
1/4 of Rs.23,100/- works out to Rs.5,775/-.

Income for consideration is Rs.17,325/-
(23,100 - 5,775).
Annual income works out to Rs.2,07,900/- (17,325 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '15'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.31,18,500/- (2,07,900 X 15).
25. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2021) 11 SCC 780 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others, each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/- (in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.40,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) on account of loss of spousal consortium, parental consortium and loss of love & affection.

Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- (in view of the Pranay Sethi case, 10%
of Rs.15,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards loss of estate.
27. FUNERAL EXPENSES:

Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.15,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards funeral expenses.

Funeral Expenses : Rs.18,150/-

Hence, petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.33,48,400/-.
29. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

30. Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 is insurer is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'
and issue No.3 is answered as 'Party in the affirmative'.
31. ISSUE NO.4 :
The petitioners No.1 to 4 are entitled for the compensation of Rs.33,48,400/-with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit together with interest, out of the compensation amount of Rs.33,48,400/- the petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for the said amount by way of apportionment as follows:
 Petitioner No.1- 20- %
 Petitioner No.2- 30 - %

7  Petitioner No.3- 30 - %
 Petitioner No.4- 20 - %
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 and 4 a sum equal to 40% shall be deposited in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.

Since the petitioner No.2 and 3 are minors, entire compensation awarded to their share shall be kept in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their parents choice till they attains the age of majority.
However the said petitioner No.1 to 4 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
